examples.ref: 1705, Francisco Sobrino, Dicionario nuevo de las lenguas española y francesa, volume 1, Bruxelles: F. Foppens, page 69b:

examples.text: Monſ. Ducan, Dotor de Mompeller, refiere de otro famoſo Medico Francès, que recetaba el Caphè vniverſalmente à todos ſus enfermos.
examples.ref: 1726, Benito Jerónimo Feijóo, Theatro critico universal, volume 1, Madrid: L. F. Mojados, page 129f.:
examples.english: Mr. Ducan, doctor of Montpellier, refers to another famous French doctor, who prescribed coffee to all of his patiens altogether.
examples.translation: Mr. Ducan, doctor of Montpellier, refers to another famous French doctor, who prescribed coffee to all of his patiens altogether.

examples.text: Explica las mercaderias que los Olandeſes ſacan de varias partes […] Azucar, Cafè, y Thè, Ambar, […]
examples.ref: 1740, Bernardo de Ulloa, Restablecimiento de las fabricas i comercio español, volume 1, Madrid: A. Marin, page 161f.:
examples.english: Explains the goods that the Dutch take from various places, […] sugar, coffee and tea, amber, […]
examples.translation: Explains the goods that the Dutch take from various places, […] sugar, coffee and tea, amber, […]

examples.text: La Francia estableció en sus colonias de Santo Domingo y la Martinica el comercio de café para excusarse de traerlo del Oriente
examples.ref: 18th c., Jorge Juan, Antonio de Ulloa, Noticias secretas de América, London: R. Taylor, published 1826, page 602:
examples.english: France established coffee trade on its colonies of Saint-Domingue and Martinique to avoid having to take it from the East
